Lessons.Title: Deriving the Quadratic Formula
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: derive the quadratic formula for any real ax²+bx+c=0 with a≠0 by normalizing and completing the square, and explain the discriminant and the ± branch. Original first-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 19 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/19/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/19/index.html (CC BY 4.0). This lesson develops a proof of the formula, not another unexamined memorization exercise.
Start ax²+bx+c=0 with a≠0. Divide by a: x²+(b/a)x=−c/a. Add (b/(2a))²=b²/(4a²) to BOTH sides. Left becomes (x+b/(2a))²; right becomes (b²−4ac)/(4a²). For real roots require discriminant D=b²−4ac≥0.

Taking square roots of both sides yields |x+b/(2a)|=√D/(2|a|). The two possible signs can be arranged as x=(-b±√D)/(2a) even when a<0 because ± branches exchange order. State this nuance rather than falsely assuming √(4a²)=2a for every negative a.

Independent numerical check: for 2x²−6x+4=0, a2,b−6,c4,D36−32=4, formula x=(6±2)/4 gives x2 or1. Factoring 2(x−1)(x−2)=0 confirms them. The derived formula therefore agrees with another independent method.

Student task: reconstruct each algebraic step from shuffled cards, identify where a≠0 is needed, explain the source of ± and D, then validate a numerical example with factoring. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for legitimate normalization, correct completed-square identity, sound square-root/sign handling and independent check.

KeyConcepts.Title: Normalize
KeyConcepts.Definition: For a≠0 divide ax²+bx+c=0 by a before completing.

KeyConcepts.Title: Completed square identity
KeyConcepts.Definition: Add b²/(4a²) to both sides to obtain a perfect square.

KeyConcepts.Title: General roots
KeyConcepts.Definition: The two branches combine to x=(-b±√D)/(2a) for D≥0.

CommonMistakes.Correction: Carry absolute value or absorb signs after ±.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Dividing by a without stipulating a≠0
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Then equation may be linear or undefined manipulation.
Loses one root for positive D.

SummaryPoints: The formula follows from completing a general normalized square.
For any nonzero a, both formula branches are valid with correct sign treatment.
Teacher evaluates derivation, not only final symbolic formula.
